name: JSON
summary: Minimal text format for structured data derived from JavaScript literal syntax: objects, arrays, strings, numbers, true, false and null. Defined twice (RFC 8259 / STD 90 and ECMA-404), deliberately unversioned, and the lingua franca of web APIs and configuration.

level_notes.0: JSON has no reference implementation: json.org's JSON_checker and Crockford's json2.js are historical reference code, and nst/JSONTestSuite is the de-facto conformance corpus. Level 0 therefore samples widely used parsers/serializers in many host languages, with files tagged by the part of the format they implement (lexing, number conversion, string escaping, UTF-8 validation, duplicate keys, depth limits).
level_notes.1: Two co-equal normative texts: RFC 8259 (IETF STD 90; grammar in ABNF plus interoperability guidance) and ECMA-404 (syntax only, railroad diagrams; also published as ISO/IEC 21778). They are intended to describe the same language. ECMA-262's JSON.parse/JSON.stringify, I-JSON (RFC 7493) and JCS (RFC 8785) are linked as normative profiles; JSON Pointer/Patch/Path and JSON Schema have their own catalog entries.
level_notes.2: Much of the secondary literature is about interoperability hazards (numbers, duplicate keys, invalid Unicode) and about parser engineering (SIMD, on-demand parsing).
level_notes.3: Rosetta Code has a JSON task rather than a category.
